transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light exercise like gardening about 1 week after your surgery. Just make sure to avoid anything too strenuous or heavy lifting for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that helps. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific product you have, I'd recommend checking with your GP or pharmacist to confirm it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's great to know, thank you! I am very sensitive to bright light lately. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, it's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate that advice, I'll keep an eye on it. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That would help me give you better information about what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about two weeks ago. Should I still be experiencing some blurriness?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
At two weeks, your vision should be improving and becoming clearer. Some mild blurriness can still be normal at this stage, but it should be getting better.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. If you're concerned, it's best to mention this at your next appointment or contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
